title: Recursive bisection
text: Split repeatedly while accounting for the whole graph
transcript: Split the largest current part on its induced subgraph; account for new cuts on the full graph.

title: Learning goals
text: Select the largest splittable part · Build the correct induced subgraph · Solve afresh on each subgraph
transcript:
Select the largest splittable part
Build the correct induced subgraph
Solve afresh on each subgraph
Account for the full-graph cut
Handle k that is not a power of two
Separate local balance from final capacity

title: 01 · Produce k parts using a bisection solver
text: Recursive bisection repeatedly splits one current part until there are k parts. k need not be a power of two. Starting from one part, each successful split adds one, so reaching k
transcript: Recursive bisection repeatedly splits one current part until there are k parts. k need not be a power of two. Starting from one part, each successful split adds one, so reaching k needs k−1 splits.

title: 02 · What belongs in the induced subgraph?
text: For selected vertices S, retain only edges whose endpoints both lie in S. Edges to other parts already contribute to the full-graph cut. Including them in the local degree matrix would change
transcript: For selected vertices S, retain only edges whose endpoints both lie in S. Edges to other parts already contribute to the full-graph cut. Including them in the local degree matrix would change the subproblem.

title: 03 · The split tree and labels
text: Record each parent, its children, local ordering and added cut. Labels identify parts; they do not measure quality. Swapping side names or renumbering parts leaves the grouping unchanged, so canonical comparisons sort
transcript: Record each parent, its children, local ordering and added cut. Labels identify parts; they do not measure quality. Swapping side names or renumbering parts leaves the grouping unchanged, so canonical comparisons sort members and ignore labels.

title: 04 · Account for the full cut
text: A split only separates vertices within its parent part. Previously crossing edges remain crossing. Therefore pure splitting cannot reduce the old cut; the increment is exactly the parent-internal weight newly separated by
transcript: A split only separates vertices within its parent part. Previously crossing edges remain crossing. Therefore pure splitting cannot reduce the old cut; the increment is exactly the parent-internal weight newly separated by this split.

title: 05 · Local balance is not final capacity
text: Requiring each child to contain at least 20% of its parent's vertices does not guarantee equally sized final parts. A 3/2 split followed by 2/1 yields counts 2/1/2. Unequal vertex areas can
transcript: Requiring each child to contain at least 20% of its parent's vertices does not guarantee equally sized final parts. A 3/2 split followed by 2/1 yields counts 2/1/2. Unequal vertex areas can widen the disparity.

title: 06 · Termination and failure
text: Stop at k nonempty parts, with k no larger than the vertex count. If a selected subgraph has no prefix satisfying the declared window, report infeasible rather than silently using an illegal
transcript: Stop at k nonempty parts, with k no larger than the vertex count. If a selected subgraph has no prefix satisfying the declared window, report infeasible rather than silently using an illegal midpoint.
